waves.rationale: The documentation review gate depends on all eleven cleanup tasks (real DAG edges): its REQ-03 requires the gate to pass on the repository's documentation tree at completion time.

The doc-review gate (6ce0f14e REQ-03) found 21 real defects across the whole shipped doc surface, beyond the 11 planned tasks. User approved (2026-07-10) fixing all 21 under this epic. Gate-driven rework on the doc tree, grouped into 4 disjoint-file workers.

lead_decisions.decision: The v1.0 milestone charter relocates to dev/vision/9db27a3a-charter.md; dev/vision/ is documented as forward-looking vision documents and the charter is exactly that. .jit/config.toml [item_kinds.charter] source is repointed and its derived-path comment corrected.
The two skill-eval records relocate to dev/eval/ (skill-eval-adjudication.md, lead-skills-eval-baseline.md), joining the existing dev/eval/ subtree.
docs/index.md is the surviving authoritative landing page; docs/README.md becomes a short pointer to it. index.md is the richer page and is the one dev/index.md and README.md link to.
The documentation review gate is keyed doc-review, backed by ./scripts/ai-review.sh with a new ./scripts/doc-review-prompt.md, matching the code-review / plan-review / breakdown-review pattern.

Workers do not write .jit/ except where a success criterion requires it (c7f0f690 doc relinks + config; 5514e4f5 doc relinks). The lead adds doc links, runs gates, and transitions state. This keeps eight concurrent worktrees from conflicting on .jit/events.jsonl.

Path-reference policy for the relocation: repoint live pointers (jit doc links, issue descriptions, .jit/config.toml, CLAUDE.md, README, docs/, skill evals). Leave historical records verbatim (dev/archive/**, session handoffs, and the audit-findings doc, where the old path is the finding itself).

Add a cargo-ci gate to a docs issue before re-running code-review. The reviewer skips cargo test when a succeeded cargo-ci gate exists; without it, concurrent gate runs trip the known find_available_port race (894337e2) and produce spurious test-failure findings.

User-approved (escalation): delete the dead storage::claims_log module. It had zero non-test consumers and serialized the claim-log sequence field as `sequence` while the live writer (claim_coordinator::ClaimLogEntry) uses `seq`; the duplicate made code-review read d48906de's correct storage-format doc as wrong. Deletion (cargo-ci green, 3545 tests) removed the contradiction without changing shipped docs.

Reversed LD-6 for the two f2532a2d session handoffs: repointed their skill-eval paths to dev/eval/ after code-review flagged them. f2532a2d is Done and one line was a forward-looking 'grade under <path>' instruction that 404'd. dev/archive/** and the epic's own audit-findings doc (where the pre-move path IS the finding) stay verbatim.

User-approved (2026-07-10): the doc-review gate's 21 findings are fixed as wave 4 under this epic rather than deferred, including rewriting web/README.md for the jit web UI and removing two 'not yet implemented' roadmap lists. Framed as 6ce0f14e REQ-03 gate-driven rework (no new issues); re-run doc-review to green, then complete.

No em-dash sweep. dw-d found 153 pre-existing em-dashes across its 5 files and asked whether to remove them. The doc-review gate does NOT grep em-dashes: its content-standards dimension (6) checks Mermaid diagrams and LaTeX math only, and jit-content-standards.md does not ban em-dashes. The em-dash ban is the lead's/global personal style rule, not this epic's contract; a ~150-line mechanical rewrite for zero gate benefit was declined. My wave-4 dispatch prompts overstated 'No em-dashes (gate greps —)'. Em-dashes workers removed as a side effect of narration rewrites are kept; no blanket sweep.
